column7: Biopolitik betrifft die Steuerung des Lebens durch den Staat.

column14: Another Foucauldian concept, referring to how state power manages and regulates the biological life of populations.

column7: Nach der Euphorie folgte schnell die Ernüchterung.

column14: From 'nüchtern' (sober, level-headed): 'ernüchtern' means to bring someone back down to earth. Often used after 'Euphorie' or 'Hoffnung'.

column7: Die Vergegenwärtigung der Geschichte gelingt dem Museum gut.

column13: The museum succeeds well at making history present.
column14: 'Vergegenwärtigung' comes from 'sich etwas vergegenwärtigen' (to mentally bring something present): making the past vivid.

column7: Zeitgenossenschaft verbindet Menschen unterschiedlichster Herkunft.

column12: Discussing shared historical experience across cultures
column13: Contemporaneity connects people of the most diverse origins.
column14: 'Zeitgenossenschaft' comes from 'Zeitgenosse' (contemporary): the fact of sharing the same historical era.

column7: Kant plädierte für ein Weltbürgertum.

column13: Kant advocated for a cosmopolitan citizenship of the world.
column14: 'Plädieren für' takes the accusative: 'für ein Weltbürgertum', a Kantian philosophical concept of perpetual peace and universal citizenship.

column7: Wir gehören alle zur selben Menschheitsfamilie.

column13: We all belong to the same human family.
column14: 'Gehören zu' takes the dative: 'zur selben Menschheitsfamilie', a fixed structure for expressing collective belonging.

column7: Die Weltgemeinschaft muss gemeinsam handeln.
column8: La comunità mondiale deve agire insieme.
column9: 'Weltgemeinschaft' unisce 'Welt' (mondo) e 'Gemeinschaft' (comunità), usato spesso nel discorso diplomatico internazionale.
column13: The world community must act together.
column14: 'Weltgemeinschaft' combines 'Welt' (world) and 'Gemeinschaft' (community), often used in international diplomatic discourse.

column7: Der Klimaschutz ist eine Menschheitsaufgabe.

column9: 'Menschheitsaufgabe' unisce 'Menschheit' (umanità) e 'Aufgabe' (compito): una sfida che riguarda l'intera specie umana.
column12: Discussing challenges facing all of humanity
column13: Climate protection is a task facing all of humanity.
column14: 'Menschheitsaufgabe' combines 'Menschheit' (humanity) and 'Aufgabe' (task): a challenge concerning the entire human species.

column7: Große Nationen tragen eine besondere Weltverantwortung.

column12: Discussing the global responsibilities of powerful nations
column13: Great nations bear a special responsibility toward the world.
column14: 'Tragen' means figuratively 'to bear, take on (a responsibility)', a common use of the verb.

column7: Die Menschenwürde ist unantastbar.

column13: Human dignity is inviolable.
column14: The first article of the German Basic Law: 'Die Würde des Menschen ist unantastbar', one of the constitution's most-cited principles.

column7: Die Unantastbarkeit der Menschenwürde ist unumstößlich.

column13: The inviolability of human dignity is irrefutable.
column14: 'Unumstößlich' means 'unshakeable, incontestable', a very high-register adjective for absolute principles.

column7: Marx beschrieb den Menschen als Gattungswesen.

column12: Discussing early Marxist philosophy of human nature
column13: Marx described the human being as a species-being.
column14: A central concept of the young Marx, referring to the essentially social and creative nature of the human being as a species.

column7: Der Selbstverwirklichungsdrang treibt viele Künstler an.

column7: Der Chef bekräftigte seine Entscheidung vor dem ganzen Team.

column13: The boss reaffirmed his decision in front of the whole team.
column14: Inseparable verb with the accusative, from 'kräftig' (strong): to make stronger, hence to confirm firmly. E.g. 'eine Aussage bekräftigen'.

column7: Kritiker sprechen von einer reinen Ellenbogengesellschaft.

column13: Critics speak of a pure elbow society.
column14: 'Ellenbogengesellschaft' combines 'Ellenbogen' (elbow) and 'Gesellschaft' (society): a society where everyone elbows their way forward.

column7: Unter Kollegen herrscht manchmal Futterneid.

column12: Discussing workplace jealousy over resources or recognition
column13: Among colleagues, professional jealousy sometimes prevails.
column14: Literally 'envy over food' (from the animal world): used figuratively for jealousy tied to resources or recognition at work.

column5: to object to, to complain about

column13: The customer objected to the quality of the goods.

column7: Futterneid unter Kollegen vergiftet das Betriebsklima.

column12: Discussing how workplace jealousy poisons morale
column13: Professional jealousy among colleagues poisons workplace morale.
column14: 'Vergiften' takes a direct accusative object, meaning 'to poison', used figuratively for a damaged social climate.

column7: Konkurrenzneid ist unter Geschwistern weit verbreitet.

column7: Geschwisterrivalität ist ein normaler Teil des Aufwachsens.

column14: 'Geschwisterrivalität' combines 'Geschwister' (siblings) and 'Rivalität' (rivalry), a psychological term from child development.

column7: Die Zahlen sind gestiegen, demzufolge wird das Team vergrößert.

column6: partner di una fase della vita (termine ironico-burocratico)

column14: An ironic, bureaucratic-sounding term coined in the 1980s, used jokingly for a non-permanent partner, almost sardonic.

column7: Ich gehe ohnehin in die Stadt, ich kann das Paket mitnehmen.

column14: Describes something that happens in any case, regardless. A synonym of 'sowieso', a little more formal.

column7: Sein Beziehungsstatus ist kompliziert.

column13: His relationship status is complicated.
column14: 'Beziehungsstatus' combines 'Beziehung' (relationship) and 'Status', a term made famous by social media profiles.

column7: Trennungsschmerz verblasst irgendwann.

column13: Breakup pain fades eventually.
column14: 'Verblassen' means 'to fade, weaken', a poetic verb often used for emotions that lessen over time.

column7: Seine Sturheit brachte das ganze Projekt in Gefahr.

column13: His stubbornness put the whole project at risk.
column14: 'In Gefahr bringen' is a fixed collocation meaning 'to endanger', often used in formal contexts.

column9: 'Dickköpfigkeit' unisce 'dick' (grosso) e 'Kopf' (testa): letteralmente 'testa dura', una determinazione ostinata.

column13: Despite her hardheadedness, everyone respected her.
column14: 'Dickköpfigkeit' combines 'dick' (thick) and 'Kopf' (head): literally 'thick head', a stubborn determination.

column7: Seine Beharrlichkeit zahlte sich am Ende aus.

column9: 'Sich auszahlen' è riflessivo e separabile, significa 'ripagare, dare frutti', usato per sforzi che alla fine portano risultati.

column14: 'Sich auszahlen' is reflexive and separable, meaning 'to pay off', used for efforts that eventually bear results.

column12: Talking about the costs of owning a house
column13: The upkeep of the house costs a lot of money every year.
column14: From 'instand halten' (to keep in good condition); used for buildings, machines and facilities. Repair is 'Instandsetzung'.

column7: Kinder zeigen früh einen gewissen Eigensinn.
column8: I bambini mostrano presto una certa testardaggine.
column9: 'Eigensinn' unisce 'eigen' (proprio) e 'Sinn' (senso): la tendenza a voler fare le cose a modo proprio, non necessariamente negativa.
column12: Discussing a child's early independence and stubbornness
column13: Children show a certain wilfulness early on.
column14: 'Eigensinn' combines 'eigen' (own) and 'Sinn' (sense): the tendency to want to do things one's own way, not necessarily negative.

column7: Die Trotzphase ist für Eltern anstrengend.

column9: 'Trotzphase' unisce 'Trotz' (sfida, dispetto) e 'Phase': il periodo dello sviluppo infantile caratterizzato da capricci e opposizione.

column14: 'Trotzphase' combines 'Trotz' (defiance, spite) and 'Phase': the period of child development marked by tantrums and opposition.

column7: Ihre Bockigkeit nervte die ganze Familie.

column9: 'Bockigkeit' viene da 'bockig' (imbronciato, ostinato come un caprone), un termine colloquiale affettuoso o esasperato.
column13: Her stubborn sulkiness annoyed the whole family.
column14: 'Bockigkeit' comes from 'bockig' (sulky, stubborn as a billy goat), a colloquial, affectionate or exasperated term.

column7: Seine Unnachgiebigkeit blockierte jede Einigung.

column9: 'Unnachgiebigkeit' unisce 'un-' negativo e 'nachgeben' (cedere): un rifiuto assoluto di scendere a compromessi.
column13: His inflexibility blocked every agreement.
column14: 'Unnachgiebigkeit' combines the negating 'un-' and 'nachgeben' (to yield): an absolute refusal to compromise.

column7: Kompromisslosigkeit kann sowohl Stärke als auch Schwäche sein.

column14: 'Sowohl ... als auch' is the fixed structure for 'both ... and', expressing that two qualities coexist in one thing.

column7: Zu viel Nachgiebigkeit wird oft ausgenutzt.

column9: 'Ausgenutzt werden' è passivo, usato per descrivere come una qualità positiva può essere sfruttata da altri.

column14: 'Ausgenutzt werden' is passive, used to describe how a positive quality can be exploited by others.

column7: Endlich zeigte er Rückgrat.

column12: Praising someone for finally standing their ground

column14: 'Rückgrat zeigen' is a fixed idiomatic expression for 'having the courage of one's convictions', literally 'showing the spine'.

column7: Charakterstärke zeigt sich in schwierigen Momenten.

column13: Strength of character shows itself in difficult moments.
column14: 'Sich zeigen in' takes the dative: 'in schwierigen Momenten', a fixed structure for indicating where a quality manifests.

column13: Fragmentation into petty states characterized Germany before 1871.

column7: Solche Kleinkariertheit hat in einem globalen Markt keinen Platz.

column14: 'Kleinkariertheit' comes from 'kleinkariert' (small-checkered, i.e., petty): a narrow, pedantic mindset.

column12: Criticising narrow, insular thinking in a debate

column14: 'Vorwerfen' takes the dative of the criticized entity and the accusative of the accusation, as in 'jemandem etwas vorwerfen'.

column14: 'Beharrungsvermögen' combines 'beharren' (to persist) and 'Vermögen' (capacity), a physics term applied metaphorically to institutions.

column7: Der Reformstau belastet die Wirtschaft.

column9: 'Reformstau' unisce 'Reform' und 'Stau' (ingorgo): un accumulo di riforme necessarie ma mai attuate.

column14: 'Reformstau' combines 'Reform' and 'Stau' (traffic jam): a backlog of necessary but never-implemented reforms.

column7: Bürokratismus lähmt viele Verwaltungen.

column13: Bureaucratism paralyzes many administrations.

column7: Manche kritisieren die europäische Regulierungswut.

column14: 'Regulierungswut' combines 'Regulierung' and 'Wut' (rage, figuratively 'excessive mania'): a critical excess of regulations.

column7: Blinder Aktionismus löst selten echte Probleme.

column14: 'Aktionismus' critically describes frantic, superficial action without an underlying strategy.

column7: Die Empörungsindustrie lebt von schnellen Urteilen.

column14: 'Leben von' takes the dative: 'von schnellen Urteilen', a fixed structure for indicating what something draws its sustenance from.

column13: Many citizens suffer from scandal fatigue.
column14: 'Leiden an' takes the dative: 'an Skandalmüdigkeit', a fixed structure for expressing suffering tied to a social phenomenon.

column7: Systemmüdigkeit macht sich in vielen Demokratien breit.
